name: Infantile-onset Generalized Dyskinesia with Orofacial Involvement
aliases: Early-onset generalized dyskinesia with facial involvement
Pediatric generalized dyskinesia with orofacial manifestations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Infantile-onset Generalized Dyskinesia

criteria.description: Onset of generalized dyskinesia symptoms before 2 years of age
Presence of involuntary orofacial movements including grimacing, tongue protrusion, and lip smacking
Exclusion of acquired or secondary causes of dyskinesia by clinical and laboratory evaluation
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with infantile dyskinesia syndromes
Partial or complete response to dopaminergic or anticholinergic therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: infantile onset, generalized dyskinesia with orofacial involvement, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may aid diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical presentation is key.

searchTerms: tube feeding through nose in infancy

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests excluding metabolic causes
CSF neurotransmitter analysis may show abnormalities in dopamine metabolites
imaging: Brain MRI typically normal or may show nonspecific basal ganglia signal changes
other: Electromyography may show dystonic muscle activity
Video documentation of involuntary movements useful for diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Brief, sudden attacks triggered by movement

redFlags: Rapid progression of dyskinesia with loss of developmental milestones
Failure to respond to standard symptomatic treatments
references: Mencacci NE, et al. Infantile-onset generalized dyskinesia: clinical and genetic characterization. Mov Disord. 2022.
Orphanet: Infantile-onset generalized dyskinesia with orofacial involvement (ORPHA:494526)
